truthAudit.Summary: Run 1 reported 14 findings. Of the 20 enumerated true vulnerabilities, Run 1 fully identified 10 (SC-V3-001, 003, 004, 005, 006, 007, 009, 010, 011, 020), partially identified 1 (SC-V3-013, found the exact code and anchors but classified it as command injection rather than insecure temp file handling), and missed 9 (SC-V3-002 integer overflow in factorial, SC-V3-008 path traversal, SC-V3-012 thread-unsafe timestamp cache, SC-V3-014 persistent auth state, SC-V3-015 unhandled exception in variable parsing, SC-V3-016 integer underflow in memory-pool block split, SC-V3-017 unbounded recursion, SC-V3-018 data race in result cache, SC-V3-019 TOCTOU in config loading). Run 1 made no false-positive findings; all 14 reported items are real defects present in the source, but 3 are additional findings outside the ground-truth set (off-by-one in safe_string_copy CWE-787, execute_admin_command command injection CWE-78, and the latent format_string template CWE-134). No evidence laundering occurred. The main systematic error is severity under-scoring: Run 1 rated several Critical issues as High/Medium (SC-V3-001, 003, 004, 009) and several High issues as Medium (SC-V3-010, 011), plus a CWE mislabel on the auth backdoor (CWE-287 vs CWE-511) and a classification mismatch on the temp-file issue (CWE-78 vs CWE-377).

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: runtime_log_format() defaults to LOG_FORMAT ('%s') but can be overwritten via set_runtime_log_format() from a config file ('log_format'). An attacker controlling the format string can use %n/%x to read or write memory.
Items.Notes: Run 1 finding #4 ('Format string vulnerability in log_debug_message', CWE-134) quotes printf(active_format.c_str(), user_input) and correctly identifies the runtime_log_format() path. The vulnerability was fully found; only severity was under-scored (High vs Critical).

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: Not reported in Run 1; the summary enumerates only buffer overflows, off-by-one, format strings, command injection, EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE backdoor, hardcoded secret, weak token, data race, use-after-free, and division-by-zero.
Items.Notes: No finding references the factorial lambda (result *= i) or integer overflow. The fact() closure at lines 312-320 accumulating into a long long is never analyzed. Genuinely missed.

Items.PreviousOutputQuote: cleanup() calls stage_deferred_history_flush() to enqueue tasks that use pool-allocated scratch after a 25ms sleep, then immediately calls g_memory_pool.cleanup() which frees the blocks; queued/running tasks then read freed memory (crash or exploitation).
Items.Notes: Run 1 finding #12 ('Use-after-free in deferred history flush vs pool cleanup', CWE-416) precisely describes the stage_deferred_history_flush -> enqueue -> sleep -> cleanup ordering. Fully found; severity under-scored (Medium vs Critical).
